entries.title: Katiba Institute v President of the Republic of Kenya & Others
entries.principle: Security concerns cannot be used as a blanket justification for curtailing constitutional rights; the state must show a reasonable and proportionate nexus between the measure and the security aim.
entries.facts: Katiba Institute challenged the President\
entries.holding: Security concerns cannot be used as a blanket justification for curtailing constitutional rights; the state must show a reasonable and proportionate nexus.

entries.title: Mubel Welfare Society v Kenya Airports Authority
entries.principle: Forced relocation that strips individuals of shelter, basic humanity and decency violates the right to dignity; resource constraints cannot excuse indignity.
entries.facts: Evicted residents of Mitumba village sought redress for forced eviction without notice or consultation. The State had reclaimed the land for airport expansion. The case raised questions of dignity, housing rights and the State\
entries.holding: Forced relocations that strip individuals of shelter, basic humanity and decency violate the right to dignity; resource constraints cannot excuse indignity.
entries.judges: Mwilu DCJ, Ibrahim, Wanjala, Ndung'u and Lenaola SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: Haki Na Sheria Initiative v Inspector General of Police & Others
entries.principle: A curfew or security order is reasonable only where it is proportionate to the threat and does not disproportionately burden an identifiable group; blanket measures require justification.
entries.facts: A petition challenging a curfew order imposed in Garissa, Wajir and Mandera counties. The petitioners alleged that the curfew was discriminatory. The case raised questions of proportionality and equality.
entries.holding: A curfew or security order is reasonable only where it is proportionate to the threat and does not disproportionately burden an identifiable group.

entries.title: Law Society of Kenya v Cabinet Secretary, Ministry of Health & Others
entries.principle: Restrictions on rights during a public-health emergency must be reasonable and proportionate; the state cannot use a crisis to impose indefinite or arbitrary limitations.
entries.facts: The Law Society of Kenya challenged the COVID-19 curfew and related restrictions. The petitioners alleged that the restrictions were disproportionate. The case raised questions of proportionality and the limitation of rights during emergencies.
entries.holding: Restrictions on rights during a public-health emergency must be reasonable and proportionate; the state cannot use a crisis to impose indefinite or arbitrary limitations.
entries.judges: Mumbi Ngugi, Ngaah and Mrima JJ (High Court)

entries.title: British American Tobacco (Kenya) Ltd v Cabinet Secretary for the Ministry of Health
entries.principle: For public participation to be meaningful it must be informed and prior; the adequacy of participation is assessed on the facts of each case.
entries.facts: British American Tobacco challenged tobacco control regulations in Kenya.
entries.holding: For public participation to be meaningful it must be informed and prior; the adequacy of participation is assessed on the facts of each case.

entries.title: R (Miller) v The Prime Minister; Cherry and Others v Advocate General for Scotland
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: The prerogative power of prorogation is justiciable; a prorogation that frustrates parliamentary scrutiny without reasonable justification is unlawful.
entries.facts: A challenge to the Prime Minister's advice to prorogue Parliament.
entries.holding: The prerogative power of prorogation is justiciable; a prorogation that frustrates parliamentary scrutiny without reasonable justification is unlawful.

entries.title: A O v Attorney General
entries.principle: Children are the most vulnerable within society and require special protection; the state must protect children from any sort of harm.
entries.facts: A petition concerning the protection of children in conflict with the law. The petitioner alleged violations of children\
entries.holding: Children are the most vulnerable within society and require special protection; the state must protect children from any sort of harm.

entries.title: Anudo Ochieng Anudo v United Republic of Tanzania
entries.court: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The arbitrary deprivation of nationality violates the right to nationality and to recognition before the law; the State must provide an effective remedy.
entries.facts: A person was arbitrarily deprived of his Tanzanian nationality.
entries.holding: The arbitrary deprivation of nationality violates the right to nationality and to recognition before the law; the State must provide an effective remedy.
entries.judges: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: Apollo Mboya v Attorney General & 2 Others
entries.principle: The State's power to regulate must be exercised in accordance with the Constitution; arbitrary or disproportionate measures are unlawful.
entries.note: Verify the neutral citation on Kenya Law before relying on it.

entries.title: Gladys Boss Shollei v Judicial Service Commission & Another
entries.principle: The failure to give written reasons for an adverse administrative decision breaches the right to a fair hearing; natural justice requires that the affected person know the case against them.
entries.facts: The former Chief Registrar of the Judiciary challenged her removal from office. The petitioner alleged that the removal was unfair and lacked written reasons. The case raised questions of natural justice and fair administrative action.
entries.holding: The failure to give written reasons for an adverse administrative decision breaches the right to a fair hearing; natural justice requires that the affected person know the case against them.
entries.judges: Mwilu, Ibrahim, Ojwang, Wanjala and Ndung'u SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: Mitu-Bell Welfare Society v Kenya Airport Authority Ltd & 2 Others
entries.principle: Evictions must be carried out in accordance with the law, with adequate notice and in a manner consistent with human dignity; the State must provide alternative accommodation where possible.

entries.title: Republic v Public Procurement Administrative Review Board & 3 Others, ex parte Syner-Chemie Limited
entries.principle: Judicial review is available where a public body acts without jurisdiction, breaches natural justice or reaches a decision that no reasonable body could have reached.

entries.title: P O v Director of Public Prosecutions
entries.principle: It is not in the best interests of the child to be held together with adults, as this may inflict a bruise that endures for life; children require separation and humane conditions.
entries.facts: A child offender challenged being held in detention with adults. The petitioner alleged violations of children\
entries.holding: It is not in the best interests of the child to be held together with adults, as this may inflict a bruise that endures for life.

entries.title: R (UNISON) v Lord Chancellor
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: A fee regime that effectively prevents access to justice is unlawful, because the constitutional right of access to the courts cannot be removed except by express statutory language.
entries.facts: A challenge to employment tribunal fees that priced out access to justice.
entries.holding: A fee regime that effectively prevents access to justice is unlawful, because the constitutional right of access to the courts cannot be removed except by express statutory language.

entries.title: Kenya Airports Authority v Mitu-Bell Welfare Society & Another
entries.principle: The State's power to reclaim public land must be exercised in accordance with the law and with respect for the rights of occupants; arbitrary evictions are unlawful.

entries.title: Mohamed Fugicha v Methodist Church in Kenya
entries.principle: Even where there is no explicit harmful intent, a measure whose effect is exclusion or disadvantage can constitute indirect discrimination; the state must strike a balance that does not disadvantage a protected group.
entries.facts: A student appealed against expulsion from school on religious grounds. The school had expelled the student for refusing to attend religious activities. The case raised questions of indirect discrimination and religious freedom.
entries.holding: Even where there is no explicit harmful intent, a measure whose effect is exclusion or disadvantage can constitute indirect discrimination.
entries.judges: Karanja, Murgor and Mohammed JJA (Court of Appeal)

entries.title: Alex Thomas v United Republic of Tanzania
entries.court: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights
entries.principle: The right to a fair trial includes the right to be tried within a reasonable time; excessive delay violates the Charter.
entries.facts: A detainee claimed violation of the right to a fair trial within a reasonable time.
entries.holding: The right to a fair trial includes the right to be tried within a reasonable time; excessive delay violates the Charter.
entries.judges: African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights

entries.title: R (Evans) v Attorney General
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: A certificate overriding a tribunal's disclosure order must be justified by cogent evidence; executive override of judicial decisions demands the highest scrutiny.
entries.facts: A request for disclosure of Prince Charles's letters to government ministers.
entries.holding: A certificate overriding a tribunal's disclosure order must be justified by cogent evidence; executive override of judicial decisions demands the highest scrutiny.

entries.title: Communications Commission of Kenya & 5 others v Royal Media Services Ltd & 5 others
entries.principle: Regulatory action affecting media freedom must be anchored in law and pursue a legitimate aim; the Court emphasised pluralism and freedom of expression while affirming the regulator's statutory mandate.
entries.facts: The Communications Commission of Kenya and media houses disputed the migration from analogue to digital television broadcasting. The dispute concerned the allocation of frequencies and the must-carry obligations. The case raised questions of media freedom, regulatory independence and the constitutional protection of expression.
entries.holding: Regulatory action affecting media freedom must be anchored in law and pursue a legitimate aim; the Court emphasised pluralism and freedom of expression while affirming the regulator's statutory mandate.
entries.judges: Mutunga CJ, Ibrahim, Ojwang, Wanjala and Ndung'u SCJJ (Supreme Court)

entries.title: Lohe Issa Konate v Burkina Faso
entries.citation: App no 4/2013 (ECOWAS Community Court of Justice, 5 November 2014)
entries.principle: Access to information is not absolute; limitations must satisfy legality, legitimate aim and proportionality, and custodial sentences for expression are disproportionate.
entries.facts: A journalist was convicted of criminal defamation in Burkina Faso.
entries.holding: Access to information is not absolute; limitations must satisfy legality, legitimate aim and proportionality, and custodial sentences for expression are disproportionate.

entries.title: R (Lord Carlile of Berriew) v Secretary of State for the Home Department
entries.court: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom
entries.principle: In national-security matters the court affords the executive a margin of judgment, but the decision must still be rational and supported by evidence.
entries.facts: A challenge to the exclusion of an Iranian dissident from the UK.
entries.holding: In national-security matters the court affords the executive a margin of judgment, but the decision must still be rational and supported by evidence.

entries.title: Toll Collective Consortium v South African National Roads Agency SOC Ltd
entries.principle: Confidentiality in respect of sensitive commercial information is a valid consideration where disclosure would undermine the implementation of a lawful transaction.
entries.facts: A challenge to the confidentiality of commercial information in a toll road concession.
entries.holding: Confidentiality in respect of sensitive commercial information is a valid consideration where disclosure would undermine the implementation of a lawful transaction.

entries.title: Trusted Society of Human Rights Alliance v Mumo Matemu
entries.principle: Parliamentary oversight mechanisms are legitimate and sufficient to rubber-stamp government functions where the process is transparent and accountable.
entries.facts: A petition by the Trusted Society challenging the appointment of Mumo Matemu as EACC chairperson.
entries.holding: Parliamentary oversight mechanisms are legitimate and sufficient to rubber-stamp government functions where the process is transparent and accountable.
entries.judges: Koome, Kihara and Murgor JJA (Court of Appeal)

entries.title: Democratic Party v Secretary General of the East African Community
entries.principle: States retain a discretionary latitude in the implementation of policy decisions; public participation must be informed and prior, but the Treaty prescribes no fixed timeline or method.
entries.facts: The Democratic Party challenged the EAC Secretary General over public participation in the admission of South Sudan.
entries.holding: States retain a discretionary latitude in the implementation of policy decisions; public participation must be informed and prior, but the Treaty prescribes no fixed timeline or method.

entries.title: Martha Karua v Attorney General of the Republic of Kenya
entries.principle: Where a partner state violates a treaty obligation, the Court may award compensation; the violation of rights under the Treaty attracts a remedy.
entries.facts: Martha Karua challenged the Kenyan government before the EACJ.
entries.holding: Where a partner state violates a treaty obligation, the Court may award compensation; the violation of rights under the Treaty attracts a remedy.

entries.title: Trusted Society of Human Rights Alliance v Attorney General & 2 others
entries.court: High Court of Kenya (Constitutional and Human Rights Division)
entries.principle: Constitutional interpretation begins with the text and structure and is informed by the values in Article 10; substantive review asks whether the process and outcome comport with the Constitution, not merely whether legal power existed.
entries.facts: The Trusted Society of Human Rights Alliance challenged the appointment of Mumo Matemu as chairperson of the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission. The petitioner alleged that the appointment process was flawed and that the appointee lacked the requisite integrity. The case raised questions of substantive review of public appointments under the 2010 Constitution.
entries.holding: The Court held it had jurisdiction; the petitioner had locus standi; the petition was not moot. On the merits, the appointment of the interested party passed constitutional muster: the process followed the Constitution and the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Act, and the integrity issue was adequately considered by Parliament. The petition was dismissed with no order as to costs.
entries.judges: Joel Ngugi, Mumbi Ngugi and G.V. Odunga JJ (High Court)

entries.title: T K v Lithuania
entries.principle: The relevant time for assessing whether a real risk of persecution exists is the time of the ongoing proceedings; claims of risk must be supported by evidence of continuing persecution.

entries.title: Olajide Afolabi v Federal Republic of Nigeria
entries.principle: Computer programs are protected as literary works under Article 2(1) of the Berne Convention, read with Article 10(1) of the TRIPS Agreement.
entries.facts: A challenge to the protection of computer programs under intellectual property law.
entries.holding: Computer programs are protected as literary works under Article 2(1) of the Berne Convention, read with Article 10(1) of the TRIPS Agreement.
entries.note: Cited in the transcript as 'Solomon v Nigeria'; principle restated as it appears in the EAC round.

entries.title: R (Bancoult) v Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs (No 2)
entries.principle: The prerogative power to legislate for a colony is subject to judicial review for rationality and conformity with fundamental rights.
entries.facts: A challenge to the removal of the Chagossians from the British Indian Ocean Territory.
entries.holding: The prerogative power to legislate for a colony is subject to judicial review for rationality and conformity with fundamental rights.

entries.title: R (Nadarajah) v Secretary of State for the Home Department
entries.court: Court of Appeal of England and Wales
entries.principle: A public authority must honour its published policies unless there are good reasons not to; legitimate expectations arise from clear and unambiguous representations.
entries.facts: A challenge to the Home Secretary's change of policy on removal of failed asylum seekers.
entries.holding: A public authority must honour its published policies unless there are good reasons not to; legitimate expectations arise from clear and unambiguous representations.

entries.title: R (Quintavalle) v Secretary of State for Health
entries.principle: Statutory language is interpreted by its ordinary meaning in context; where the text is ambiguous, purposive construction may extend it to new circumstances.
entries.facts: A challenge to regulations permitting the creation of embryos by cell nuclear replacement.
entries.holding: Statutory language is interpreted by its ordinary meaning in context; where the text is ambiguous, purposive construction may extend it to new circumstances.

entries.title: R v Secretary of State for the Home Department, ex parte Brind
entries.principle: At common law the intensity of review is limited: proportionality is not a general domestic ground of review, and courts afford the decision-maker a margin of judgment in policy-laden fields.
entries.facts: The Home Secretary banned the broadcasting of statements by terrorist organisations; journalists challenged the ban.
entries.holding: At common law the intensity of review is limited: proportionality is not a general domestic ground of review, and courts afford the decision-maker a margin of judgment in policy-laden fields.

entries.title: Velasquez Rodriguez v Honduras
entries.principle: The duty to protect requires the State to act diligently; alleging that investigations have commenced is not sufficient — the State must show concrete measures taken.
entries.facts: A challenge to the disappearance of a student in Honduras.
entries.holding: The duty to protect requires the State to act diligently; alleging that investigations have commenced is not sufficient — the State must show concrete measures taken.

entries.title: Additional Protocol II to the Geneva Conventions
entries.citation: Protocol Additional to the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949, and relating to the Protection of Victims of Non-International Armed Conflicts (1977)
entries.principle: Extends Common Article 3 protections in non-international armed conflicts of sufficient intensity between State forces and organised armed groups.

entries.title: Padfield v Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food
entries.principle: A discretion conferred by statute must be exercised in furtherance of the policy and purposes of the Act; it may not be used to frustrate the object for which it was granted.
entries.facts: The Minister refused to refer a complaint about milk marketing to a committee of investigation.
entries.holding: A discretion conferred by statute must be exercised in furtherance of the policy and purposes of the Act; it may not be used to frustrate the object for which it was granted.

entries.title: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, Article 12
entries.principle: Freedom of movement may be restricted only where provided by law and necessary to protect national security, public order, public health or morals, or the rights of others.

entries.title: Ridge v Baldwin
entries.principle: The rules of natural justice — a fair hearing before an impartial tribunal — apply to administrative and disciplinary decisions affecting rights or legitimate expectations.
entries.facts: A chief constable was dismissed without a hearing; he challenged the dismissal.
entries.holding: The rules of natural justice — a fair hearing before an impartial tribunal — apply to administrative and disciplinary decisions affecting rights or legitimate expectations.

entries.title: Geneva Conventions, Common Article 3
entries.principle: In non-international armed conflicts, each party must treat humanely persons taking no active part in hostilities; violence to life and person, cruel treatment and outrages upon personal dignity are prohibited.

entries.title: Associated Provincial Picture Houses Ltd v Wednesbury Corporation
entries.court: Court of Appeal of England and Wales
entries.principle: A decision is reviewable where it is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority, having regard to the relevant considerations, could have reached it; irrelevant considerations and bad faith also vitiate.
entries.facts: A local authority refused a cinema licence for Sunday opening; the cinema owner challenged the refusal.
entries.holding: A decision is reviewable where it is so unreasonable that no reasonable authority, having regard to the relevant considerations, could have reached it.

entries.title: British and Irish Legal Information Institute (BAILII)
entries.principle: Free access to UK judgments cited as persuasive authority under section 3 of the Judicature Act.
entries.note: Free access to UK judgments cited as persuasive authority under section 3 of the Judicature Act.

entries.title: Civil Procedure Act (Cap 21) and Rules
entries.principle: General procedural framework; rules are made under the Act and published as subsidiary legislation.
entries.note: General procedural framework; rules are made under the Act and published as subsidiary legislation.

entries.title: Judicature Act (Cap 8)
entries.principle: Section 3 receives the common law, equity and statutes of general application in force in England on 12 August 1897 — the basis on which UK authority is persuasive.
entries.note: Section 3 receives the common law, equity and statutes of general application in force in England on 12 August 1897 — the basis on which UK authority is persuasive.

entries.title: Supreme Court Act, 2011
entries.principle: Governs the Supreme Court's jurisdiction, including the advisory jurisdiction under Article 163(6).
entries.note: Governs the Supreme Court's jurisdiction, including the advisory jurisdiction under Article 163(6).
